The Court also requested the tribunals to decide the disputes expeditiously, preferably within 3 months. Since the Court had already constituted election tribunals headed by former judges to deal with such disputes, it said that there was no reason to adopt a different approach in the case of the BCD elections. It accordingly disposed of the petitions, granting aggrieved parties liberty to approach the election tribunals. items.title: Arundhati Roy: ‘Message from Jantar Mantar is bigger than electoral defeat’
items.summary: In a wide-ranging interview with Newslaundry , Arundhati Roy discusses the Hindi translation of her new book, Meri Maan, Meri Gangster , which draws on the story of her mother, Mary Roy, to explore her own childhood, family, relationships, and journey to becoming a writer. The conversation, however, went beyond the book to address contemporary politics and student movements as well. Roy spoke at length about leaving home at 16, studying architecture in Delhi, her friendships, and the early days of her writing career. She describes her mother as a woman who was both “extraordinary” and “extremely harsh”, and explains why it’s essential to see her not merely as a mother, but as an independent woman in her own right. The conversation then proceeded to the recent student protests at Jantar Mantar, the state of the education system, Hindutva politics, elections, democratic institutions, the movements in Narmada and Bastar, the environment, and social inequality. Roy argues that the current student movement can’t be understood merely through the lens of exams and education. Watch the full conversation. Small teams can do great things. Tharahai Cuthbert ]. Justice D Bharatha Chakravarthy was dealing with an election petition filed by a rival candidate who believed he should have received more votes because of his work in the constituency. The Court observed that it is ultimately the electorate that decides whom to vote for. The mere belief that a candidate's public service should have fetched him more votes cannot be a ground to doubt the counting process, it said. " It may be true that he has done good work. Vinod Tomar, the WFI’s former assistant secretary, was acquitted of the remaining charge against him. The court held that the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. items.title: Advocates acting as insolvency professionals liable to collect, deposit GST: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has ruled that advocates acting as insolvency professionals are liable to collect Goods and Services Tax (GST) from recipients of their services and deposit it with the government under the forward charge mechanism [Kanwal Chaudhary v. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India]. A Division Bench of Justices Prathiba M Singh and Shail Jain held that advocates providing insolvency and receivership services must obtain GST registration and comply with the requirements applicable to insolvency professionals as a class. “ An Advocate acting as an Insolvency Professional would, therefore, be governed by the ‘forward charge mechanism’, which is applicable to Insolvency Professionals, as a class, and not by the ‘reverse charge mechanism’, which is otherwise applicable to Advocates rendering legal services ,” the Court said. Justice Prathiba Singh and Justice Shail Jain Under the forward charge mechanism, the service provider adds GST to the invoice, collects it from the recipient and deposits it with the government. Under reverse charge, the recipient of the service is responsible for depositing GST. The Court clarified that its ruling applies only to services rendered

items.title: Freedom at Midnight: Kerala HC refuses to entertain PIL against exclusion of men at women-only event
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Thursday refused to entertain a public interest litigation (PIL) petition challenging restrictions on entry of men to the 'Freedom at Midnight' event slated to be organised for women and children by the State government [Adarsh SR v State of Kerala & anr] The program planned by Department of Women and Child Development is scheduled to be held from 10 pm on August 14 to 1 am on August 15 from PMG Junction to Overbridge Junction in Thampanoor area of Thiruvananthapuram. It is a symbolic event aimed at allowing women to safely reclaim public spaces while celebrating the Independence Day. However, the plea filed by a lawyer said the prohibition on entry of men in the area violates their fundamental rights to equality and free movement. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice Syam Kumar VM said the petition was filed on the basis of an unverified press report. Pertinently, it recorded the State's submission that the restriction applied only to the entry of men to the women's conclave and that there was no plan to prevent them from using public roads. items.title: Bombay HC grants relief to ex-TISS student booked for raising slogans supporting Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam
items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Friday granted interim protection from arrest to a former Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS) student accused of allegations that he raised inflammatory slogans including slogans supporting jailed activists Sharjeel Imam and Umar Khalid at an unauthorised campus event. [ Kamakhya Das v. State of Maharashtra & Ors. ]. Justice Prafulla Khubalkar noted that the electronic devices belonging the accused Kamakhya Das were already seized and custodial interrogation would not be necessary at this stage. Hence, the judge granted bail to Das while asking him cooperate with the ongoing investigation. "Considering the nature of the allegations and the fact that the mobile phone and laptop of the applicant are already seized, at this stage, custodial interrogation need not be insisted upon. Hence, the interim protection granted by the trial court needs to be continued further, subject to certain conditions," the judge held. Das was directed to attend the concerned police station on August 19 and 24 between 10 am to 2 pm.
